open_obligations: Check whether Smit et al. measure how often debates converge on wrong answers.
Note the main effect is reported for Multi-Persona, not Du et al.'s Society of Minds.
Check that the best agreement setting is chosen without test-set leakage.
out.other_title: Debates can converge confidently on an incorrect answer
out.rationale: Du et al. report debates can converge on a wrong answer and that agents are relatively agreeable. Smit et al. report prompted agreement intensity significantly affects Multi-Persona accuracy, with high agreement best for MedQA and PubMedQA and strong disagreement best for counter-intuitive CIAR; this bears on premature wrong consensus but measures accuracy, not convergence.
out.scope: proposed ADDRESSES: whether controlling how readily agents agree changes debate outcomes, for GPT-3.5-turbo multi-agent debate on QA datasets

text: The paper reports that agreement intensity has a significant effect on Multi-Persona's accuracy, acting through agreement in the first debate round. MedQA and PubMedQA benefit from high agreement while CIAR shows the reverse pattern, which the authors attribute to CIAR being counter-intuitive so that strong disagreement raises the chance of reaching the correct answer.
title: Best agreement level depends on dataset: high for MedQA, low for counter-intuitive CIAR
